name: Stack
description: A flex primitive that stacks children along one axis with consistent spacing and alignment.

anatomy.description: A flex root that lays children out along one axis; direction defaults to column.
Even spacing between children; numbers follow the spacing scale (n × 0.25rem), strings pass through as CSS lengths.
align and justify map to cross-axis and main-axis flexbox values.
An optional flag that lets a row flow onto multiple lines.

dos: Use numeric gaps from the spacing scale so the rhythm stays consistent with the rest of the UI.
Combine wrap with direction="row" for toolbars and tag rows that must survive narrow widths.
Nest Stacks to compose simple two-axis layouts before reaching for Grid.
donts: Don't use Stack for two-dimensional track layouts; use Grid or Columns.
Don't space children with margin utilities; set gap on the Stack so spacing stays uniform.
Don't expect equal-width cells; Stack children size to their content.

examples.title: Axis and spacing
examples.description: Numeric gaps follow the spacing scale; direction, align, justify, and wrap map to flexbox.

examples.title: Vertical rhythm
examples.description: The default column direction stacks header, content, and footer blocks with even spacing.

examples.title: Wrapping rows
examples.description: wrap lets a row flow onto multiple lines on narrow screens.

guidance.useWhen: Children flow along one axis with even spacing, from toolbar rows to page-level vertical rhythm.
guidance.avoidWhen: The layout needs two-dimensional tracks or equal-width cells; use Grid or Columns.
guidance.behavior: Numeric gaps follow the spacing scale (n × 0.25rem); direction, align, justify and wrap map straight to flexbox, and the as prop can swap the rendered element.
guidance.responsive: Combine wrap with row direction so toolbars reflow onto multiple lines; switch direction per breakpoint through responsive classes.

notes: Stack is purely visual; the DOM order is the reading order, so keep the source order meaningful.
Use the as prop to render a semantic element (nav, ul) when the grouping has meaning.
